items.detail: Every route but the probes and the two public routes takes the owner's bearer credential, compared in constant time; a rejected credential is never echoed back.
items.label: One authenticated owner

items.detail: GET /health and GET /ready need no credential and are answered before load is shed.
items.label: Liveness and readiness probes

items.detail: GET /v1/routes and GET /v1/routes/<alias> render the operator's identifiers and nothing else; a limit the source did not report stays absent.
items.label: Read-only route inspection

items.detail: GET /v1/models lists each model with its wires and max_model_len, without a credential and without waking a pod. Since 0.6.0.
items.label: Public model listing

items.detail: GET / answers the Codex, Claude Code or Loom settings for each model, chosen by User-Agent, and never the owner secret. Since 0.6.0.
items.label: Setup instructions per client

items.detail: Every refusal code, status and message, and every numeric bound, is checked against the published contract.
items.label: Published refusals and bounds

items.detail: A drain reports unready while it keeps serving; a stop answers every accepted request before it returns.
items.label: Graceful drain and stop

items.detail: The gateway crate's whole dependency closure is itself: nothing in it can resolve a secret, reach an upstream or create a resource.
items.label: No secret, upstream or provisioning in the gateway library

items.detail: The owner's POST to /v1/chat/completions, /v1/responses or /v1/messages reaches the target the embedding hands out and streams back as it arrives; only the top-level model is rewritten.
items.label: Chat, Responses and Messages wires relayed by the library

items.detail: A non-empty top-level tools array for a model whose tool_calling is absent is tools-not-served, decided before any target is asked for.
items.label: A tool request to a model without tool calling is refused before a pod starts

items.detail: An effort of high or max becomes xhigh, the deepest the served Qwen3.8 template accepts; adaptive thinking and output_config.format pass unchanged; anthropic-version and anthropic-beta are dropped. Settled from Claude Code's documentation and vLLM v0.27.1's source, not a live session.
items.label: Claude Code's Messages requests reach vLLM in a form it serves

items.detail: A hosted model may declare reasoning_effort low, medium or xhigh; a Messages request that names no effort reaches the endpoint with output_config.effort set to it, so a server started by hand does not think at its template's xhigh default. A named effort, the other wires and Runpod models are unchanged.
items.label: A hosted model's declared effort reaches its endpoint when a request names none

items.detail: For a model with a window (a Runpod model's max_model_len, a hosted model's context_window), the input is counted at the target's /v1/messages/count_tokens; a max_tokens above the room left is lowered to it, and an input that leaves none is context-exceeded, whose message Claude Code compacts on. A count that fails relays the request unchanged. Settled from vLLM v0.27.1's source, not a live session.
items.label: A Messages request never asks for more output than the window has room for

items.detail: The usage block of a target's answer reaches the client byte for byte on the Chat and Messages wires, streamed or not: vLLM's cached_tokens, cache_read_input_tokens and cache_creation_input_tokens, and any field the gateway does not know. Settled from vLLM v0.27.1's source and authored answers, not a live server.
items.label: Usage details reach the client unchanged

items.detail: A connection failure or a 502, 503 or 504 answers upstream-failed and drops that endpoint; the next request reaches a replacement.
items.label: A failed target is dropped and replaced

items.detail: A request for a model whose pod is starting waits up to request_hold_seconds, then is model-cold-start with retry-after 30. Tested through a seam over the emulator.
items.label: Cold-start hold in the Runpod composition

items.detail: A provider's daily_cap_usd and total_cap_usd are checked before every pod create against the reported spend and the pods' estimates; a start that would pass one, or whose spend is unknown, is spend-ceiling with no create. Tested over the emulator; the live spend read needs a connectors release that offers billing.pods.
items.label: Spend ceilings on pod starts

items.detail: A model may declare ordered profiles, each GPU types with their vLLM settings; when Runpod refuses every create of a profile for capacity the start moves on to the next profile inside the same startup deadline and spend check, and the usage record names the profile that served. Tested over the emulator.
items.label: Model profiles with capacity fallback

items.detail: POST /v1/models/<alias>/wake starts a Runpod model's pod as a request would, through the same spend check and profile fallback, and answers 202 at once; it starts nothing more while the pod starts or serves. GET /v1/models/<alias>/status answers stopped, starting (with the provider's sub-phase), ready or stopping and the profile, from the pool's records, with no provider call. Both take the owner credential; a hosted model has neither and is path-unknown. Tested over the emulator.
items.label: Wake a model and read its phase

items.detail: The binary starts a model's pod through the connectors CLI and relays to its https proxy URL, verifying the certificate against the Mozilla roots compiled in before any request byte. Tested against a connectors fixture and a loopback https pod, not against Runpod.
items.label: Relay to a Runpod pod from the binary over verified TLS

items.detail: A model declared as [hosted.<alias>] is relayed to any server that speaks its wire at an http or https base URL, with a bearer, an API key in a named header, or no credential, read from a file. https is verified against the same roots as a pod. Tested against loopback endpoints, not against a vendor API.
items.label: Hosted endpoints

items.detail: A hosted endpoint's base path replaces the wire path's leading /v1, so https://openrouter.ai/api/v1 is asked on /api/v1/chat/completions and a base URL ending in /v1 works as written; host stays the authority. A path with an empty, . or .. segment, a query, a fragment or user information is refused at start. Tested against loopback endpoints.
items.label: A hosted base_url may carry a path

items.detail: [hosted.<alias>.headers] declares non-secret request headers, such as anthropic-version or X-Title, sent with every request to that endpoint. Framing headers, authorization and the endpoint's credential header are refused at start, and client headers are still never forwarded. Tested against loopback endpoints.
items.label: Static headers per hosted endpoint

items.detail: An OpenCode Go endpoint is sent the client's own valid x-opencode-session, else llmgw- and a hash of the client's address under a per-process key, else the declared static one; a malformed client value is never sent, and no other endpoint gets one. Tested against a TLS fixture endpoint, not against OpenCode Go.
items.label: One OpenCode Go session per client

items.detail: A [hosted.<alias>] model of kind = "bedrock" is served by llm's Bedrock client: region, model or inference-profile id, InvokeModel for an Anthropic id and Converse otherwise, every request signed with SigV4 from the container credentials endpoint (Amazon EKS Pod Identity). Chat tool turns stream their tool-call deltas or answer whole. A field Bedrock does not take is dropped and its name logged. Tested against a fixture Bedrock Runtime and credentials endpoint, not against AWS.
items.label: Amazon Bedrock models

items.detail: Claude Code's claude -p turn on the Messages wire reaches a Bedrock model through InvokeModel and is answered on the Messages wire, its signed thinking carried back on the tool-result turn. Tested against a fixture Bedrock Runtime with a captured request shape, not a live session.
items.label: Claude Code on a Bedrock model

items.detail: A Messages client's anthropic-beta names reach an InvokeModel model's body as anthropic_beta, in the client's order, only when the model's anthropic_beta list names them; every other name is dropped and logged by name, and a malformed header to such a model is refused translation-invalid before anything is sent. A Converse model, a model without a list and a chat or responses client are sent none, the header unread. Tested against a fixture Bedrock Runtime, not against AWS.
items.label: Anthropic beta names on a Bedrock model

items.detail: A request on a wire the model's upstream does not speak is decoded with llm 0.19.0, checked and projected before any target is asked for, sent with llm's client for the model's first declared wire, and answered on the client's wire, streamed event by event with the upstream's usage. A field outside the subset, carried reasoning state and an unrepresentable answer are refused by name. Tested against loopback fixture upstreams, not a vendor API.
items.label: Translation between wires within llm's subset

items.detail: Each translation-unsupported or translation-invalid refusal writes one info line naming the model, the client's wire, the code and llm's diagnostic, which names the refused path or field and never a value the client sent; a key the client chose outside the subset is written ?, and the names the contract lists as refused by name stay named. The answer still carries only the code. Tested on each client wire with a marker in the request's values and in a secret-shaped key, at the root and nested, that no log line and no answer carries.
items.label: A translation refusal names the refused field in a log line

items.detail: Claude Code's first turn reaches a chat or responses upstream, and Codex's first turn a chat or messages upstream, with their effort, thinking, parallel tool calls and cache and verbosity hints under the upstream wire's names; effort max reaches chat and responses as xhigh. Claude Code's later turn, which replays reasoning another upstream minted, is still refused translation-opaque-state. Tested with captured client requests against loopback fixture upstreams, not a vendor API.
items.label: Claude Code's and Codex's first turns on a translated route

items.detail: GET / hands Codex and Claude Code a profile for a model whose upstream speaks another wire when the client's recorded first turn translates to it under the model's capabilities, and none when it is refused; the gateway asks once, at start, and logs nothing for it. Claude Code's profile for such a model turns its structured output off, which every translated path refuses, with the setting its published gateway protocol names; that setting has not been observed against a live client. A Loom run is profiled only for models that declare chat. Tested through the binary against loopback fixture upstreams, not a vendor API.
items.label: Client setup for translated routes

items.detail: A translated answer to a responses client carries the upstream's reasoning state sealed for its route under a key the gateway generates at start and never writes out; the next turn on that route is served, a messages upstream getting back the thinking block it signed and a chat upstream the turn without it. An item from another route or wire, an altered or forged seal and one sealed before a restart are refused translation-opaque-state. No seal reaches a messages client. Tested with Codex's captured two-turn exchange against loopback fixture upstreams, not a vendor API.
items.label: Codex's later turns on a translated route

items.detail: routes = "<path>" serves each route of an llm.routes/1 document under its name from its endpoint: relayed byte for byte on the endpoint's wire to its base path, translated from the other wires under the route's capabilities, beside [models.*] and [hosted.*]. Credentials come only from file: key files read through the trusted reader; env: and keychain: secrets, a base_url without its API path and an alias collision are refused at start. Tested against loopback endpoints, not against a vendor API.
items.label: The models of an llm.routes/1 document

items.detail: ingress_auth = "none" serves the three wire paths without a credential, for a gateway behind something that authenticates already, and the binary warns before it listens. The counters and the route inventory still take the owner secret, and refuse everything when there is none. bearer, the default, is unchanged.
items.label: Model calls without a credential, on request

items.detail: b10x-llm-gateway --config <file>: an unknown key at any level is refused as config:schema, naming its line and the keys allowed there.
items.label: One closed TOML deployment document

items.detail: The document, the routes document it names, the owner secret, each vLLM key file and each endpoint credential file are opened once, never through a symlink, and checked for owner, mode, size and UTF-8 on that one handle.
items.label: Trusted-file reader

items.detail: b10x-llm-gateway credential set --config <file> --model <alias> (or --route <name>) reads the key from a hidden prompt or --stdin, probes GET <base path>/models with the entry's own credential header and static headers (401 or 403 stores nothing), and writes the file the document names, mode 0600, read back through the server's own reader before it replaces the old one. Tested against loopback endpoints, not against a vendor API.
items.label: Store an upstream key with credential set

items.detail: A model may name vllm_api_key_file; the key is read once at startup and written nowhere.
items.label: A vLLM key file per model

items.detail: The binary answers what it accepted, prints the accepted and completed counts, and exits 0.
items.label: Stop on SIGINT or SIGTERM

items.detail: The root Dockerfile builds a distroless, non-root image of b10x-llm-gateway on port 8080. No image is published.
items.label: Container image definition

items.detail: Prometheus text behind the owner credential, under llmgw's series names, so an llmgw scrape keeps working.
items.label: llmgw's 13 counters at /metrics

items.detail: llmgw_request_duration_seconds{model}, a histogram with fixed buckets from 0.05 to 300 seconds, and llmgw_requests_total{model,outcome}, outcome one of ok, upstream_error, timeout and refused; every model registered at zero, labelled only by its alias and fixed words.
items.label: Latency and outcomes per model

items.detail: metrics_listen binds a second listener that answers GET /metrics and nothing else, without the owner secret; metrics_bearer_file makes a scrape send its own token.
items.label: A scrape listener without the owner secret

items.detail: Relayed, refused or upstream-failed, each request makes one record; the binary writes it as one tracing event at info. Token counts are always absent.
items.label: One usage record per authenticated wire request

items.detail: Provider-assigned identity, one lease at a time, stop obligations that only a complete inventory discharges, and an in-process FakeProvider.
items.label: Hosting lifecycle contract

items.detail: One pod per model under concurrent first requests, GPU fallback in declared order, crash and deadline termination, idle reaping and an orphan sweep, against EmulatedRunpod.
items.label: Runpod vLLM pool over an emulator

items.detail: ConnectorsRunpod creates, lists and terminates pods only through the connectors CLI, each write with an approval proof for its exact input. Tested against a fixture of that CLI, not against Runpod.
items.label: Runpod transport through the connectors CLI

items.detail: The system llm-gateway is specified in ESS; the gate answers at least 387 of 387 scenarios, skips none, and fails on drift between the specification and its generated suite.
items.label: ESS specification and conformance suite

items.detail: A model with ordered targets tries the next one when an attempt fails before any answer byte reaches the client.
items.label: Fallback to the next target

items.detail: Each usage record carries the token counters and the model name the target reported; a count it did not report stays absent.
items.label: Token counts in usage records

items.detail: One recorded live session per client against a model on a real Runpod pod through the binary. Nothing is qualified yet.
items.label: Live sessions of Claude Code, Codex and Loom

items.detail: b10x-llm-modal exports nothing yet.
items.label: Modal adapter

source: llm-gateway-docs, from its capability list; every shipped item names the test that holds it
